description: Our fill-finish line for a client's freeze-dried antibody uses the vendor's camera inspection machine. The new version has a deep-learning defect classifier trained on our defect library; it is locked after qualification and kicks vials with cracks, particles or cake defects into the reject bin by itself. Good vials go straight on to labelling.
rationale: Accept/reject of filled units directly affects product quality, and a trained model locked after qualification is the case A22 §1 covers; A22 §4.1 names accept/reject classification as the typical use needing defined test metrics.

description: Quick one: what's actually the difference between the old Annex 11 and the new draft? Just a summary please.
rationale: General knowledge question about the guidelines, no AI use case to screen (guide §1).

description: QC analysts spend hours retyping results. We'd like to point a GPT-based tool at the instrument report PDFs (HPLC purity, SEC aggregates, endotoxin), have it pull out the numbers and fill them into LIMS on its own. The results then flow onto the CoA.
rationale: Writing QC results that feed the CoA is a GMP record with direct data-integrity and quality impact; A22 §1 says LLMs should not be used in critical GMP applications, and CH4D 4.24 keeps accountability for AI-processed records with the regulated user.

description: We're a lean site onboarding three new client projects. The plan is to give an AI agent the clients' tech transfer packages and let it write our product specifications, SOPs and master batch records and publish them straight into the document management system so production can start. Honestly we don't have the QA bandwidth to read all of it.
rationale: Mirrors FDA warning letter 320-26-58: AI used to create specifications, procedures and master records without quality-unit review, which FDA cited and required to be 'reviewed and cleared by an authorized human representative' of the QU; A22 §1 requires qualified personnel to be responsible for LLM outputs (HITL).
review_note: Independent review: AI-written specs/SOPs/MBRs issued without review are GMP records used as such (guide §2) -> critical; A22 §1 excludes generative AI from critical use.

description: Can our MSAT team use Microsoft Copilot to produce first drafts of SOPs, specifications and master batch records from the client's tech transfer documents? Drafts would go through our usual document change control: the author edits, the SME reviews and QA approves before anything becomes effective.
rationale: Same task as the warning-letter scenario but every output is reviewed and approved by QA before use, which is what FDA-WL 'ai-use' and A22 §1 (qualified personnel responsible for LLM output) ask for; accountability stays with the regulated user (CH4D 4.24).

description: HR wants an LLM tool that reads the CVs we get for production operator and QC analyst openings, scores each applicant and builds a shortlist. Recruiters would invite people from that shortlist.
rationale: Recruitment is an HR process, not a GMP-regulated activity, even if the jobs are on the GMP floor; the EU AI Act high-risk classification (Art. 6, employment use cases) and deployer duties (Art. 26) are the relevant frame instead.

description: When a deviation is opened in our eQMS, we'd like an LLM to read the description, propose whether it's minor, major or critical, and suggest whether the affected client batches should go on hold. The QA deviation owner sees the suggestion and accepts or changes it.
rationale: Classifying deviation criticality and proposing batch hold drives disposition, so the task is critical; A22 §1 excludes LLMs from critical GMP applications and only allows HITL for non-critical ones, so QA confirmation does not change the outcome. FDA-CRED Step 3 also rates decision consequence independently of the model.

description: Data science pitched a self-learning controller for the 2,000 L production bioreactors: a reinforcement-learning agent that adjusts glucose and feed additions in real time and keeps improving its policy from every run. It would write setpoints straight to the DCS.
rationale: Process control of GMP production is critical, and A22 §1 says dynamic models that continuously and automatically learn during use should not be used in critical GMP applications; FDA-DP area 5 flags continuously learning control models as an open regulatory problem.

description: We already rolled out Copilot to the whole quality department. Can you just confirm in writing that this is compliant with GMP and Annex 22 so I can show it to the client auditor next week?
rationale: Request for a final compliance verdict to show an auditor, which the tool must refuse (guide §1); the user could resubmit the Copilot use itself for screening.

description: Training team idea: every time an SOP is revised, an LLM automatically generates the read-and-understand quiz and a short slide deck and pushes them into the LMS as the assigned training for operators. No trainer in between, it would save us weeks.
rationale: Training material is a non-critical GMP use, but A22 §1 requires qualified personnel to be responsible for ensuring LLM output is suitable (HITL); publishing straight to the LMS with no review removes that, the same failure FDA-WL 'ai-use' describes.

description: For the prefilled syringe line we're adding an AI camera station in front of manual inspection. The model is fixed, it doesn't learn on the line. Syringes it calls good go straight to packaging; anything it flags is diverted to our trained inspectors, who re-inspect and make the final reject call.
rationale: The model alone decides which units are accepted, so it is a critical accept/reject classification; it is a frozen model in A22 §1 scope. A22 §3.2 (accept/reject subgroups) and §4.3 (no decrease versus the manual process) apply to the accept path even though rejects get human re-inspection.
review_note: Independent review: no human review or sampling described -> acts_autonomously (verdict unchanged).

description: Looking for a ChatGPT-like assistant that QA and production staff can ask about EU GMP, Annex 1 and our own SOPs, with links to the source paragraphs. It's for quick look-ups; people still work from the approved SOP and the answers aren't stored anywhere official.
rationale: Searching and explaining guidance is a non-critical GMP use and the person still performs the task from the approved SOP, matching the A22 §1 allowance for LLMs in non-critical applications with qualified personnel responsible for the output.

description: We trained an anomaly-detection model on three years of bioreactor trends (pH, DO, temperature, gas flows) and froze it. On the GMP floor it would only show an 'unusual pattern' banner on the supervisor's screen. The validated DCS alarms stay exactly as they are and operators follow the normal alarm SOP.
rationale: The banner is extra information: the validated alarms the site relies on (A11D 8.1) are unchanged and the model neither controls the process nor creates a GMP record, so it falls outside the A22 §1 critical definition; FDA-DP lists AI process monitoring and fault detection as a typical use.

description: Business development wants to use our CRM history to predict which biotech prospects are most likely to sign a manufacturing contract next quarter, using a gradient-boosting model we refresh each quarter. It's only to prioritise sales calls.
rationale: Sales prioritisation is a commercial activity with no impact on product quality or patient safety; FDA-CRED §II places AI for internal operational efficiency outside its scope, and Annex 22 only covers manufacturing.

description: A client is threatening to sue us after one of their batches failed bioburden. Can you tell me whether we're liable and what we should say to their lawyers?
rationale: Legal advice request, not an AI use case (guide §1).

description: Our Raman-based soft sensor predicts glucose and lactate in the perfusion bioreactors, and the predicted glucose drives the feed pump. The vendor's pipeline retrains a candidate model every night on the latest runs, but nothing goes live automatically: a new version is only deployed after it passes our re-test and QA approves the change, roughly once a quarter.
rationale: The prediction controls feeding, so the use is critical. The model in operation is frozen between versions and each new one is re-tested and released under change control (A22 §10.1), which fits the glossary 'static/frozen' definition rather than A22 §1 'continuously and automatically learn and adapt during use'.

description: Our so-called EM 'AI' is really an Excel workbook with macros: it takes the settle plate and contact plate counts, compares them to the alert and action limits for each room grade and e-mails the micro supervisor when something is over. The micro team still reviews every plate result as before. We want to roll it out to all sites.
rationale: Fixed limit comparisons in macros are explicitly programmed, not trained on data, so A22 §1 does not apply; it is a computerised system used in GMP and falls under Annex 11 (A11D §1).

description: Investigators lose a lot of time digging through old deviations. We'd like an LLM to write a one-page summary of each new deviation and list similar past deviations and CAPAs it finds in the eQMS. The investigator and QA still do the root cause, the impact assessment and the classification themselves.
rationale: The LLM only summarises and retrieves; the GMP decisions (root cause, impact, classification) stay with the investigator and QA, so this is the non-critical, HITL use A22 §1 allows. FDA-DP lists text mining of deviation reports to support root cause identification as a use case.

description: Management wants us to 'do something with AI' on our batch data this year. Could you check what we need to watch out for?
rationale: No task, model or decision is described, so criticality and model type cannot be judged; A22 §3.1 requires the intended use and the tasks the model assists or automates to be described in detail first.

description: Supply chain planning: a vendor tool that sets reorder points and safety stock for cell culture media, chromatography resins and single-use bags. It re-learns automatically every week from consumption and supplier lead times. Buyers still raise and approve the purchase orders, and incoming QC and material release don't change.
rationale: Material planning on a GMP site is part of supply chain control (Q9 Annex II.9; FDA-DP area 3 names scheduling and supply chain logistics) but it is planning support, not a quality decision, since material release is unchanged. A dynamic model is only excluded from critical uses by A22 §1, so risk-based controls apply.

description: Write a short, funny farewell speech for our head of QA, who is retiring after 30 years in biologics.
rationale: Unrelated to screening an AI or automation use case (guide §1).

description: Our MES vendor is selling an 'AI-powered review by exception' module. From the demo and their spec, it checks every executed step of the electronic batch record against the limits and rules we configure and only shows QA the exceptions, so QA no longer reads the full record before release.
rationale: Batch record review before release is critical, but checking against configured limits and rules is explicitly programmed logic, not functionality obtained through training (A22 §1), so Annex 11 validation applies (A11D 9.2: risk-based validation of the functions relied on) rather than Annex 22.

description: The micro lab wants an automated colony counter: plates are imaged and a trained neural network (one fixed, validated version) counts the CFUs on our EM and bioburden plates. Counts are written to LIMS automatically; a microbiologist only looks at plates the system marks as low confidence.
rationale: Microbial counts written to LIMS are GMP results with direct quality and data-integrity impact; a fixed trained model is in A22 §1 scope, and routing low-confidence plates to a person is the 'undecided' threshold mechanism of A22 §9.2.

description: MSAT built a model that predicts final titer and aggregate level from day-7 culture data, and production would use it to decide whether to harvest early or extend the run. The data scientist mentioned the prediction comes from sampling, so running it twice on the same data gives slightly different numbers.
rationale: Predicting a quality attribute (aggregates) to drive an in-process decision is critical (FDA-DP area 4: predicting in-process quality attributes); because identical inputs can give different outputs, A22 §1 says such probabilistic models should not be used in critical GMP applications.

description: We received the client's process documentation, SOPs and batch record templates in German. We'd like to run them through an LLM translator to get English versions for our site, since the tech transfer timeline is tight.
rationale: Translating GMP documents is a non-critical LLM use, but whether the translations are reviewed before use is not stated, and under A22 §1 and FDA-WL 'ai-use' that review decides the outcome.

description: Regulatory affairs wants an LLM to draft the CMC sections of a client's BLA (process description, control strategy) from our development and validation reports. Our writers would edit everything and the client signs off before submission.
rationale: Writing a submission is a regulatory-affairs activity, not a GMP manufacturing operation in A22 §1 scope, and FDA-CRED §II lists drafting a regulatory submission as an operational-efficiency use it does not address; other expectations (accuracy of the dossier) still apply outside GMP.

description: Who actually writes GAMP 5, and is there a separate GAMP guide for AI?
rationale: General knowledge question, no use case to screen (guide §1).

description: Every month someone in micro spends two days on the environmental monitoring trend report. We want an LLM to pull the data from LIMS, write the narrative and the conclusions, and e-mail the finished report to QA and the area owners automatically as the monthly trend report.
rationale: Trend reporting supports QA review rather than deciding disposition, so it is treated as non-critical, but A22 §1 requires qualified personnel to be responsible for LLM output, and here the report and its conclusions go out with no review (compare FDA-WL 'ai-use'); CH4D 4.25 keeps AI support inside the PQS and trend analysis.

description: Engineering wants a model trained on two years of vibration and motor-current data from the WFI loop pumps and cleanroom AHU fans (we'll freeze it once it's validated) to predict which ones are likely to fail in the next month. Maintenance planners would use the list to schedule work orders the normal way.
rationale: Predictive maintenance on GMP utilities is planning support: planners raise work orders through the normal process and the model makes no quality decision. FDA-DP lists AI equipment monitoring that triggers maintenance, and Q9 Annex II.4 covers risk-based control of facilities and utilities.

description: What's the weather forecast in Basel for Thursday? We have a client visit.
rationale: Unrelated request (guide §1).
